culture.vibe: Laid-back Californian surf culture. UCSB is famous for its relaxed vibe — students study hard but also surf, bike to class, and socialise on the beach. Isla Vista (adjacent neighbourhood) is one of the most social student areas in California.
culture.thingsToDo: Surfing at Goleta Beach (walking distance), biking along the coast, kayaking, Santa Barbara farmers markets, wine country day trips, hiking in the Santa Ynez Mountains, whale watching, State Street restaurants.
culture.socialScene: Very social campus. Large student population but feels intimate due to coastal setting. International students welcomed — strong surf and outdoor culture. Less city-oriented than LA but more relaxed.
culture.olivierMatch: ★★★★★ Closest climate and lifestyle to Sydney in entire guide. Beach at your doorstep. Relaxed atmosphere. Less urban bustle than LA but arguably better day-to-day liveability for an Australian.

facilityDetails.stadium: Harder Stadium — 17,000 capacity, on-campus, IAAF-certified 8-lane track surrounding natural grass soccer field. Home of Santa Barbara Sky FC (USL League One, 2025).
facilityDetails.trainingFields: 2 practice fields adjacent to Harder Stadium. 1 additional satellite training field on east campus. All-weather surfaces, permanent floodlighting. Santa Barbara climate allows year-round outdoor training.
facilityDetails.strengthConditioning: UCSB Athletics Weight Room — 15,000 sq ft shared facility with strength coaches for all Olympic sports. Free weights, Olympic platforms, Keiser pneumatic systems. Soccer-specific conditioning blocks scheduled with dedicated S&C coach.
facilityDetails.sportsScience: Exercise Science teaching labs with metabolic carts (VO2 max), body composition analysis (DEXA), and functional movement screening. GPS tracking via Statsports system on all training sessions. Video analysis system (Hudl) with iPad tablets for all players.
facilityDetails.sportsMed: Dedicated athletic trainer for soccer. On-site treatment room with ultrasound, e-stim, ice baths. Goleta Valley Cottage Hospital sports medicine partnership for imaging and surgical consultation.
facilityDetails.academicLabs: UCSB Department of Kinesiology: teaching labs for biomechanics, motor learning, exercise physiology. Bren Hall science facilities available to kinesiology students. Marine Science Institute provides additional lab access. Pre-PT advising formally integrated into kinesiology program.
facilityDetails.extras: UCSB Recreation Center (one of the most highly rated campus rec facilities in the USA) — climbing wall, Olympic pool, fitness studios. Team video room in Harder Stadium. Beach volleyball courts, surfboard rental, ocean swimming all on campus.
facilityDetails.note: Largest stadium capacity in the guide. Hosted NCAA College Cup in 2010 and 2018. Now shares with USL League One professional club. UC system provides strong S&C and sports medicine support. Elite stadium presence for a Big West program.

fin.internationalNote: Cal Poly SLO non-resident direct billed cost $58,854 (2026-27, Tier-1 verified from Cal Poly Financial Aid's official Undergraduate Costs of Attendance 2026-27, New Student enrolling fall 2026, Residence Hall): California base tuition and fees $14,682 for the College of Science and Mathematics (where Kinesiology sits) + non-CA resident tuition $14,130 + the non-CA Resident Opportunity Fee $8,804 = $37,616, plus housing $12,682 and meals $7,656, plus the $450-per-semester international student fee ($900). NO credit-load assumption was needed — Cal Poly itself labels the line '30u @ $471/unit'. ⚠ THE OPPORTUNITY FEE IS THE STORY: $8,804 a year charged only to non-California residents, on top of the per-unit surcharge, and it is easy to miss because it sits in a separate 'in addition to the fees above' table. Cal Poly's own headline non-resident total for this college is $63,238; mandatory international health insurance is extra and excluded by convention. Engineering, Architecture and Agriculture pay $1,038 more. The previous stored $32,000 was an unresearched ballpark and understated the cost by $26,854 — the LARGEST error found anywhere in this campaign. Cal Poly is not a cheap CSU for a non-resident; the value lens falls 44 to 28 accordingly.

name: UC San Diego
kinRank: Good (Human Biology, B.S. — no Exercise Science or Kinesiology major exists at UCSD)
acuAlignNote: UCSD has no "Exercise and Rehabilitative Sciences" degree — that name appears nowhere associated with the university. The previously stored "EDS" course codes are real at UCSD, but EDS stands for Education Studies, a completely unrelated department — the fabrication reused a real prefix with invented course titles ("EDS 117 — Human Anatomy" etc. don't exist; real EDS 117 is an Education Studies course). The real, closest match is Human Biology, B.S. (Biological Sciences), which covers human physiology and biochemistry and the molecular basis of disease — but has no confirmed exercise-specific curriculum. UCSD Health remains a genuine clinical resource for a general pre-health pathway.

fin.internationalNote: Cal State Fullerton non-resident direct billed cost $42,292 (2026-27, Tier-1 verified from CSUF Financial Aid's official 2026-27 Undergraduate Cost of Attendance table, Non-California Resident Students / On-Campus residence hall column): non-resident tuition $12,246 + mandatory tuition $6,838 (stored together under `tuition` = $19,084, as the CSU splits the systemwide base from the per-unit non-resident surcharge) + campus fees $1,678 + housing $14,890 + food $6,640. CSUF's own headline on-campus non-resident total is $48,394, adding books, miscellaneous, transportation and loan fees that this guide excludes. The non-resident surcharge is $471 a unit and the $12,246 reflects CSUF's OWN stated basis of 13 units a semester — not an assumption made here; a 15-unit load would add about $1,884 a year. The previous stored $28,000 was an unresearched ballpark and understated the cost by $14,292. Orange County living costs are high. Athletic aid is the main lever; CSU merit aid is limited.
